title: Sovereign immunity and required parties
summary: Sovereign immunity can prevent a state or foreign sovereign from being joined in litigation without an applicable exception or waiver. When that sovereign claims an interest in the dispute, its absence also affects the Rule 19 analysis.
notes: Rule 19 remains a contextual analysis, but the immunity and sovereign interest can give dismissal unusual force. This is not a rule that every absentee has the same protection as an immune sovereign.

sections.Meaning: Sovereign immunity can prevent a state or foreign sovereign from being joined in litigation without an applicable exception or waiver. When that sovereign claims an interest in the dispute, its absence also affects the Rule 19 analysis.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the immunity, the asserted interest, whether joinder is possible, and the practical effect of a judgment without the sovereign. Pimentel shows why a court cannot resolve the sovereign’s property claim against it merely as a preliminary justification for proceeding.
